market_sizing.target_buyer: Operations director, plant manager, or owner-CEO. Co-packers >$5M revenue almost always have an ops director. Below that, the owner signs and the QA/production manager evaluates.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Estimated 300-500 contract food manufacturers / co-packers in AU. Visible names: Mansfields (QLD), Carewell Group, PakCo, Food Processing Specialists, Maltra Foods, Formulated For You, Wholesale Food Group, OzScientific (consulting + production), Brownes (dairy co-pack). Long tail of co-mans embedded in commercial kitchens (~200+) under $2M revenue. ensun's 'Top 100 Food Manufacturing Companies in Australia (2026)' is the closest census proxy. [uncertain] on exact total.
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: ~3,000 co-packers (Contract Packaging Association ~600 members + long tail). UK: 400-700. NZ: 50-100. CA: 200-400. All [uncertain].
market_sizing.typical_size: 10-200 employees, AU$2M-$50M annual revenue. The Manuva sweet-spot is sub-AU$10M (10-50 staff).
market_sizing.growth_trend: Steady 4-7% segment growth driven by brand-owner outsourcing. FSANZ + FSMA 204 (extended past Jan 2026 by 30 months) is a tailwind for traceability investment. Private-label growth in AU supermarkets (Coles/Woolworths house brands) drives co-packer demand. AU manufacturing SMB count +7.0% YoY to June 2025 (ABS).

fit_and_timing.addressable_window: Now for the bottom of the segment (AU$2-5M revenue, single-site, 1-3 brand customers). After full Xero/MYOB and multi-tenant client-isolation features for the AU$5-15M middle.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: Brand-owner / client portal (each brand customer needs visibility into their inventory and batches separately). Multi-tenant isolation within a single Manuva tenant. Production scheduling / labour tracking is a soft gap. Xero/MYOB integration. FSMA-204 KDE/CTE export format is a hard requirement for any co-packer exporting to US.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Pro ($499) is the natural floor; Pro+addons or a custom Co-Pack tier ($799-1499) is more realistic for the AU$5M+ segment.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 5 — FSANZ + HACCP + state food licence + AQIS for export + FSMA 204 for US exporters + GFSI/SQF/BRCGS certification commonly required by brand-owner clients.
fit_and_timing.time_to_value_days: 30-60 days. Multi-customer setup, recipe migration, integration with Xero/MYOB, label-printing integration, and a real onboarding session are all required.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Nulogy is the dominant purpose-built co-pack tool — pricing not public but typically US$2-5K/mo + implementation. SAP Business One ~AU$2-5K/mo. NetSuite ~AU$3-8K/mo. Dynamics 365 BC ~AU$1.5-4K/mo. SYSPRO ~AU$1.5-3K/mo. PEPPOL-ready food ERPs (Sage X3, Aptean Food & Beverage) AU$2-6K/mo. Mid-tier still on MYOB Exo or NetSuite light + paper / Excel for shop floor.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$500-1500/mo realistic for sub-AU$10M co-packers if Manuva closes the FSMA-204 export + client-portal gaps. Below $500 is non-credible for a co-packer buyer — perceived as too lightweight.
economics.estimated_arpu_aud: AU$650/mo blended (Pro tier + likely paid Co-Pack add-on).
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 5 — Multi-site fees, per-brand-client fees, FSMA/SQF audit-pack add-on, scheduling module, labour-tracking add-on. Single largest expansion-revenue segment.
economics.churn_risk: 2 — Co-packers, once embedded, are very sticky. Switching cost is enormous (recipe library, label templates, audit history, brand-owner relationships). 1-2% monthly churn typical for vertical ERPs in this segment.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$500-1500 (industry events, content, paid LinkedIn); founder-time CAC ~40-80 hours per close (long discovery + reference visits + pilot scoping) at $150/hr = $6,000-12,000. Blended AU$6,500-13,500.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: ~1.6-3.4:1 with founder-time loaded — marginal to healthy. Becomes very healthy (10:1+) once a partner-channel motion (food ERP consultants) lowers founder-time CAC.
economics.typical_seat_count: 8-30 (operations, QA, warehouse, production planning, sales, finance, brand-owner liaison).
economics.multi_channel_count: 1-2 channels per co-packer for their own products (most co-packers are services businesses, not brand-owners). 'Channels' for this segment really means 'brand-owner clients' — 5-30 per site.
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 95-100% B2B — the entire revenue model is wholesale to brand-owners.

Manufacturers' Monthly. Smart Industry Expo attendees.

where_they_live.industry_facebook_group_size: Approx 5-15K aggregate across food manufacturing AU FB groups. LinkedIn is the dominant channel — FB is weaker for B2B-services audiences. [uncertain]

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — Co-packer ops directors are findable on LinkedIn but gate-kept by gatekeepers (admin, plant secretary). Email open rates lower than SMB. Cold-call to plant works for SMB co-packers (<50 staff). Long sales cycle.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — 'FSMA 204 compliance for AU co-packers', 'Nulogy alternative comparison', 'SQF audit-ready batch tracking' are high-intent SEO targets. Whitepapers and FoodLegal-style explainers convert this buyer.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 2 — Lowest founder-market-fit score in the Tier-A set. Co-packer buyers expect deep food-industry credibility: GFSI/SQF familiarity, recall-drill experience, brand-owner relationship language. Solo outsider founder will struggle without a Food-Innovation-Centre champion or an AFGC-member advisor lending credibility.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: High — first 5 references likely require 6-9 months and at least one paid pilot per logo at AU$5-15K each.

foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Free trial does not fit this segment — co-packers will not deploy on free trial. Paid pilot (AU$2-5K for 3 months + scoping doc + named SuccessOwner) likely converts 40-60% based on Nulogy / Aptean / Crafted ERP industry norms. [uncertain]
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Paid pilot ONLY — AU$2-5K for 3 months, credited 100% on conversion to annual contract. Pair with a credible AU food-industry advisor (ex-AFGC, ex-FIAL, ex-Mansfields) as fractional GTM partner to clear the credibility bar. Inbound through 'FSMA 204 for AU co-packers' SEO + whitepaper gated downloads. Founder-led discovery sessions but with the advisor on the call. Do not attempt free trial / design partner for this segment without industry-credibility cover.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 3 (months 9-15+). Wait until Manuva has 10+ paying customers in adjacent food segments (11, 14) to demonstrate FSANZ track-record. Co-packers are the highest-ARPU, highest-LTV prize but the worst solo-founder fit early.

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Nulogy is the global purpose-built leader for co-packers (~25-35% of $10M+ co-packers globally; lower in AU where penetration is partial). SAP Business One, NetSuite, Dynamics 365 BC, SYSPRO hold the rest of the AU mid-market. Aptean Food & Beverage and Sage X3 are emerging. AU$2-5M long tail is mostly MYOB Exo + paper / Excel on the shop floor. Crafted ERP is starting to appear in beverage-adjacent co-packers. [uncertain] on exact AU splits.
competitive_context.switching_pain: 5 — Highest switching pain of any segment in this study. Recipe library, label templates, audit history, integration with brand-owner EDI, SQF/BRCGS document control — all migration-heavy.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Nulogy: enterprise pricing locks out sub-AU$10M co-packers, US/UK-centric, no AU FSANZ-native reports. SAP B1 / NetSuite: too generic, weak on multi-customer batch/recipe isolation. MYOB Exo: no shop-floor, no batch traceability, no FSMA 204. Manuva can close: (a) AU$500-1500 price point for sub-AU$10M co-packers, (b) multi-customer batch isolation, (c) FSANZ + FSMA 204 export, (d) Xero/MYOB native AU.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Nulogy G2/Capterra: complaints about implementation complexity, slow customisation, lack of mid-market pricing. AFGC member feedback (anecdotal) on cost of enterprise food ERPs. Reddit r/foodscience and r/manufacturing occasional 'Nulogy alternative' threads (global). [uncertain] on direct quotes — most public satisfaction data is mixed and segment-anecdotal.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Fragmented at AU SMB level (no tool >25%); Nulogy + SAP B1 + NetSuite together cover ~55% of the AU$10M+ segment.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Xero, MYOB, SAP/NetSuite (for clients with brand-owner integration requirements), GS1 Australia (barcoding/SSCC), Zetes / Videojet label printers, EDI (BPC, Truecommerce), Coles/Woolworths brand-owner portals, Quikspak / SQF Institute audit tools, FSMA 204 KDE/CTE format, freight (Mainfreight, Linfox EDI).

partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: AFGC corporate membership ~AU$15-50K/yr (too high for solo founder); AFGC newsletter slots ~AU$1-3K. FIAL partnership programs ~AU$5-25K. AUSPACK sponsorship AU$5-50K. Fine Food Australia booth AU$10-30K. Manufacturers Australia ~AU$2-5K. Food Innovation Centres (FIC) partnership programs are the best low-cost inroad — most state FICs offer free-or-cheap visibility to vendors that bring real value to members. [uncertain] on exact 2026 rates.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 1-3 paying customers in 12 months under solo-founder constraint. Realistic only if Manuva commits a senior food-industry advisor and a paid-pilot motion in months 6+.
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Co-packers alone cannot land AU$3-5K MRR inside 12 months for a solo founder — too long a cycle. Path if attempted: (1) recruit one credible food-industry advisor (ex-AFGC / ex-Mansfields-tier name) as fractional GTM partner in exchange for equity or revenue share, months 0-3; (2) build FSMA 204 + multi-customer batch isolation MVP, months 3-9; (3) ship paid-pilot offer to 10 hand-picked AU$2-5M co-packers, months 6-12; (4) close 1-2 paid pilots at AU$650 + AU$5K pilot fee. Realistic MRR contribution: AU$1-2K by month 12.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~128 customers at AU$650 blended ARPU. Highest-LTV path — co-packers are the closest segment to the AU$1M ARR aspirational ceiling if Manuva builds the co-pack module out.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 1 — Worst bandwidth fit in the Tier-A set. Each onboarding consumes 40-80 hours; support burden is heavy; multi-customer isolation features can drag development for months.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 10-14 months on cash CAC; 18-28 months with founder-time loaded.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: High erosion — co-packers expect named SuccessOwners, quarterly business reviews, audit-prep assistance. Effective GM 55-65% rather than 80%+ until product matures.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 4 — Defer to Phase 3. Highest ARPU/LTV but worst solo-founder fit and longest path to revenue. Strategic prize once Manuva has 30-50 customers, founder credibility, and one named advisor.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) Credibility gap is severe — solo founder without food-industry CV will be filtered out at gatekeeper stage. (2) Multi-customer isolation is a non-trivial product investment (~3-6 months engineering) that adds tech-debt and bloat to the broader SMB product. (3) FSMA 204 extension (now ~July 2028) reduces urgency of the export-compliance hook. (4) Nulogy mid-market push could close the wedge before Manuva ships. Verify before going hard: actual AFGC member appetite for a sub-AU$1500/mo co-pack tool; whether a named advisor would partner; whether multi-customer isolation can be served via tenant-per-brand instead of in-tenant isolation. STRONG RECOMMENDATION: Treat this as a Phase 3 strategic option, NOT a Phase 1 acquisition channel. The risk of building a parallel product line for one segment while the SMB book stays small is real.
